Subject: Re: [opensuse] NFS background mounts

On Thu, 2008-03-06 at 08:16 +0100, Roger Oberholtzer wrote:

> 
> autofs may be the way to deal with this. It is, however, sweeping the
> crumbs under the carpet. Using autofs does not change the fact that nfs
> is not properly waiting to do the mount in the background. Either it is
> broken or I am using it improperly.
> 
> In my case, the NFS volume will always be used right away. These systems
> are in a vehicle-based measurement system and are restarted on a regular
> basis. Still, autofs may solve my immediate problem, if not nfs's
> general issues with this. So, thanks for the suggestion.
> 

Only thing i am aware of, is that the combination dhcp & NFS is not such
a good one.

Default timeout for a lease is set at 20 seconds, and 99,9999% of the
time, that's not enough, The system continues, while leaving
dhcp-request in the background (which eeventually succeeds)
But either the nfs-client or nfs-server is started up without a proper
network address.

IF that's the case, edit /etc/sysconfig/network/config
and change the line:
WAIT_FOR_INTERFACES="20"
into
WAIT_FOR_INTERFACES="120"

(vi, yast, autoyast)
